title: OpenAI did decades of math in one release

lines.text: OpenAI just did *decades* of math in one release, | and the best mathematicians alive are *worried.*
This week, OpenAI gave an unreleased model about *4,000* open problems. | It cracked less than *10%* of them, | but that's still *372* results.
One of them is the *Unique Games Conjecture,* | which Scott Aaronson says his wife spent her *whole career* working toward.
OpenAI won't even *name* the model. | Almost every result came from *one prompt,* | with about *three hours* of thinking each.
But here's the catch. | Less than *half* of the proofs are checked by a computer, | and nobody outside OpenAI can run the model | to see *how* it got there.
And these models learned from decades of papers | mathematicians shared for *free.* | That's why *25* Fields Medal winners signed a letter | warning about *plagiarism* and *credit.*
Terence Tao says the race to be *first* should matter less, | and *explaining* a result should matter more.
Because if sharing your work just trains a model that takes the *credit,* | people might stop *sharing* it.
Want to understand AI like this, | *one lesson* a day? | Head to *Teyro.*

sources: github.com/openai/math README (read 2026-10-09): unreleased internal OpenAI model; posed approximately 4,000 problems; 372 result families (~9%); vast majority via the same procedure, averaging three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; ~42% of top-line results formalized in Lean; 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'; model not named
Decrypt (2026-10): OpenAI spokesperson: almost everything came from a single prompt to a single agent
Quanta Magazine (2026-10-07): OpenAI announced a Unique Games Conjecture proof among the results
Scott Aaronson, 'The Mathocalypse', scottaaronson.blog (2026-10-07): his wife Dana Moshkovitz spent her career working toward proving the Unique Games Conjecture
TechCrunch (2026-09-11): 25 Fields Medal winners signed an open letter: 'this raises severe attribution and plagiarism questions'; rushed announcements leave no time for citing previous work
Terence Tao on Mathstodon: 'Math 1.0' placed a premium on being the first to solve an open problem; his proposal: priority to the first to explain a result, not the first to generate it
Removed (not confirmed on a primary source): GPT-6-ASTRO / Epoch Erdős benchmark, 'Navier-Stokes needed 10,000 agents', 'written on psychedelics' quote, Miller sphere-packing credit + correction
